saints.name: St. Blaise
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A bishop of Armenia martyred under Licinius, invoked from ancient times for ailments of the throat…
biography: A physician who became bishop of Sebaste in Armenia, Blaise withdrew in time of persecution to a cavern in the wilderness, where wild beasts were said to gather tamely about him. Found there by the governor's hunters, he was brought before Agricola, who governed Cappadocia and Lesser Armenia under the Emperor Licinius.

As he was led to prison, his acts relate, a mother laid at his feet her only son, choking on a fishbone, and the child was healed; for this he is invoked against ailments of the throat. Unshaken, he was beaten, torn with iron combs, and beheaded about the year 316. From those combs' likeness to the tools of the trade he became the patron of wool-combers.

His acts were written centuries after his death, yet his cult spread widely in East and West, and he is counted among the Fourteen Holy Helpers. On his feast two blessed candles are crossed against the throats of the faithful, with the prayer that through his intercession God deliver them from every disease of the throat.
saints.knownFor: The blessing of throats given on his feast.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 3 February
